title: Zenith Retail — incident notes & customer comms draft
notes:
Summary:
- Customer: Zenith Retail (dedicated pool: eu-west-1a, pool-id: dp-zenith-01)
- Symptoms: intermittent 500/503 on /v1/generate and unexplained response truncation for chat sessions starting 2025-11-03 09:12 UTC.
- Impact window (observed): 2025-11-03 09:12 UTC -> 2025-11-03 14:20 UTC (repeat blips 11/04 morning).

Chronological breadcrumbs (raw):
2025-11-03 09:11:43 UTC — first alert: route "zenith/generate" P50 latency spike -> 1.2s (norm ~120ms).
2025-11-03 09:12:05 UTC — first 503s from edge logs (nginx): "upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response"
2025-11-03 09:13:02 UTC — internal SLO monitor: 8% error rate over 5m window.
2025-11-03 09:15:20 UTC — SRE paged; escalated to oncall eng-sre + serving-runtime.
2025-11-03 09:18:00 UTC — attached to pod: redwood-serving-zenith-0: container logs show repeated: 
  "panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference"
  "goroutine 664 [running]:
  github.com/redwood-inference/serving/runtime.(*ModelWorker).Serve(0x0, 0x... )"
2025-11-03 09:25:00 UTC — k8s reported OOMKilled for redwood-serving-zenith-1 around 09:24:58 UTC.
2025-11-03 09:27:10 UTC — scaled pool down 3 -> 2 (temporary) and drained traffic; brief reduction in errors.
2025-11-03 10:05:40 UTC — after scale back to 4, errors returned.
2025-11-03 10:22:33 UTC — noticed model binary revision mismatch across nodes: node-a: rev 2025.10.31+g8c, node-b: rev 2025.11.01+g2a
2025-11-03 10:25:00 UTC — rolled back node-b to rev 2025.10.31 image; errors reduced but not eliminated.
2025-11-03 11:40:12 UTC — curl check to local /health returned 200 but /v1/generate returned HTTP 200 with truncated JSON body "{\"id\":\"...\"\n" (malformed).
2025-11-04 07:08:22 UTC — customer reported new occurrence during EU morning ops.

Commands & outputs tried (copied raw where useful):
- kubectl describe pod redwood-serving-zenith-0 -n zenith-prod
  -> NodeAffinity: preferred, Events: BackOff 4m (x5)
- kubectl logs redwood-serving-zenith-0 -n zenith-prod --since=30m
  -> repeated runtime panics and a stack snippet: "kvcache: checksum mismatch at page 23"
- curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <masked>' https://api.redwood.com/zenith/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
  * Connected to api.redwood.com (10.0.0.5) port 443
  > POST /zenith/v1/generate HTTP/1.1
  < HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
  < content-type: application/json
  < content-length: 19
  {"error":"upstream closed"}
- strace attached to worker process reproduced "write() EPIPE" when attempting to flush response to socket.
- checked dedicated pool autoscaler config: maxSurge=1, minReadySeconds=30 ; no recent changes in policy.
- verified KMS logs around key rotation: no activity.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Model KV cache corruption after recent partial rollout. Evidence: checksum mismatch log + mismatch in model revision across nodes. Likely root cause for nil deref when cache expected non-nil pointer.
2) Serving runtime regression introduced in 2025-11-01 build: new attention kernel altered memory layout leading to occasional OOB access on certain GPUs. Evidence: panic stack + OOMs on some pods. Linked PR candidate: serving-runtime PR #1427.
3) Network path / edge pooling issue causing half-open connections and EPIPE when worker tries to write but socket closed. Evidence: nginx upstream closed messages and strace EPIPE. Less likely because local /health OK and truncated JSONs show worker produced malformed output.
4) Rate-limiter burst misconfiguration causing abrupt connection drops under bursty retail traffic; low priority given absence of 429s in logs.

Temporary mitigations applied (what worked & didn't):
- Full pool rollout rollback to image 2025.10.31 reduced crash frequency by ~70% (partial mitigation).
- Disabled prefix/KV caching on redwood-serving-zenith-* nodes (env REDWOOD_KV_CACHE=off) -> reduced checksum mismatch logs but higher per-token cost; customer ops OK with short-term cost increase.
- Added retry at edge for upstream closed (302 -> retries) for 5m; reduced 503s but not a real fix.
- Replaced node-b NVMe instance (suspected disk corruption) -> one window without errors for 12m but then reappeared.

Next steps (owned + ETA):
- eng-serving-runtime (Maya) to revert PRs in candidate list and run build with extended unit tests focusing on attention kernels (ETA: 2025-11-06).
- eng-sre (Jordan) to schedule controlled canary: 2 nodes with KV cache off, 2 nodes with cache on + fsck on kv files; monitor for checksum logs (ETA: today EOD).
- platform-engineering to run disk SMART & fio on node images and replace faulty hardware if needed (ETA: 2025-11-05).
- product/solutions: internal customer update + proposed temporary SLA credit draft (Liam) (ETA: 2025-11-05).

Draft internal note to send before customer-facing: (short)
---
Heads up: Zenith experienced intermittent 503/500s starting 11/03 09:12 UTC. Initial root cause signal points to KV-cache checksum mismatch after a partial rollout (model binary revision mismatch + serving-runtime panics). We have rolled back to stable image, disabled KV cache on the pool, and are running hardware checks. Maya is coordinating a runtime build + test. Working on customer comms and will update after the canary completes.
---

Draft customer-facing message (first-touch, informal / for review):
Subject: Update on 11/03 Zenith service disruption\n
Hi Alex / Zenith Ops team,

Thanks again for flagging the behavior this morning — we know this was disruptive and we're sorry. Quick update: our initial investigation indicates a corruption issue in the model caching layer that surfaced during a recent partial rollout. We've reverted the rollout for your dedicated pool, temporarily disabled model-KV caching to prevent further checksum errors, and are running additional hardware checks on the nodes in eu-west-1a.

What this means for you now:
- Immediate: errors should be significantly reduced; we have a short-term cost increase due to caching being disabled (we'll bill at the normal rate and discuss credits if needed).
- Short term (next 48h): we'll run a controlled canary with a fixed serving-runtime build that includes extra safety checks; we'll share the exact ETA once tests finish.
- Post-mortem: we'll share a detailed timeline and RCA within 5 business days.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute call with our SRE and runtime lead to walk through the mitigation plan.

Apologies again — we appreciate your patience.

Best,
Jordan (oncall, Redwood Inference)

Open questions / TODOs (notes for me):
- Capture full core dump from a crashing worker (need to increase core_pattern and S3 upload script).
- Add healthcheck for kvcache checksum mismatch via /internal/kvcache_health endpoint.
- Confirm whether recent kernel driver updates on NVidia side correlated with build 2025-11-01. (check with infra).
- Prepare RCA skeleton (owner: Maya) and timeline for customer PM.

Misc quick refs (for followups):
- grep -R "kvcache: checksum mismatch" /var/log/zenith/* | wc -l -> ~142 entries between 11/03 09:12 and 11/04 08:00
- tail -n 200 /var/log/nginx/zenith-edge.log | grep "upstream closed" -> repeated blocks with same timestamp pattern
- docker image tags: 2025.10.31-stable, 2025.11.01-canary

End of notes.
